decree_date_gregorian: 24 May 2010 CE (independently re-derived via the hijridate/hijri-converter library: Hijri(1431,6,10) -> 2010-05-24; matches prior research)
base_law_reference: sources/anti_narcotics/law/official_source/anti_narcotics_law_official_source.json (نظام مكافحة المخدرات والمؤثرات العقلية، المرسوم الملكي رقم م/39، 8/7/1426هـ، المادة 69)
structural_note: Flat sequence of 40 مواد (articles), numbered 1-40, no باب/فصل structure, no topical section headers (unlike the base law). Two articles (2 and 34) embed substance/dosage tables within their own مادة text rather than the Regulation being organized as a standalone substance schedule/قائمة at the top level.
verification_methodology_note:
Implementing Regulation ("Executive List") of the Anti-Narcotics and Psychotropic Substances Control Law «اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مكافحة المخدرات والمؤثرات العقلية» — approved by Council of Ministers Resolution No. 201, dated 10/6/1431H (independently re-derived via the hijri-converter/hijridate Python library: Hijri(1431,6,10) -> Gregorian 2010-05-24, i.e. 24 May 2010 CE), published in the Official Gazette on 6/7/1431H (18 June 2010 CE), entering into force 30 days after publication per the Regulation's own Article 40. This resolution's SAME enacting text also carries a second, textually distinct operative clause ("ثانيا") amending a DIFFERENT prior Council of Ministers Resolution (No. 203, 14/7/1425H, as amended by No. 186, 17/7/1426H) governing reward payments to members of the narcotics-destruction committee (لجنة إتلاف المخدرات) — that reward-schedule text is NOT part of the Implementing Regulation's own 40 articles and is excluded from the ingested article set; it is quoted in full in this artifact's preamble_ar field for transparency only. DIRECT-FETCH ATTEMPTS AND FAILURES (documented per corpus convention): (1) laws.boe.gov.sa (lawId be479758-9a84-4e94-b1d3-a9a700f19454) — both WebFetch and direct curl (with browser User-Agent, routed through the sandbox's HTTPS proxy) failed: WebFetch returned HTTP 503, and curl was terminated with 'Recv failure: Connection reset by peer'. (2) The MOI PDF (moi.gov.sa/.../Executive+list+for+drugs.pdf) — WebFetch returned HTTP 503; direct curl was also reset ('Connection reset by peer'). (3) Wayback Machine — the archive.org 'wayback/available' API (reachable) confirmed a 9 Feb 2026 snapshot of the BOE LawDetails page exists, but retrieving that snapshot's content failed via every method attempted: WebFetch returned HTTP 422/refused, and direct curl to web.archive.org returned 'Blocked by egress policy' (a sandbox-level restriction distinct from the HTTPS proxy, applying specifically to web.archive.org content-serving endpoints, not the 'available' API host). This mirrors the exact same three-way failure pattern already documented in the base law's own official_source.json for the same three fallback tiers. PRIMARY SOURCE ACTUALLY USED: nezams.com's dedicated regulation page (fetched directly via curl with a standard browser User-Agent header through the sandbox's HTTPS proxy; nezams.com returned HTTP 406 without a browser User-Agent, and 200 with one — a bot-blocking heuristic, not an access-control wall). The page presents this Implementing Regulation as a sequence of exactly 40 numbered مواد (subject-1 through subject-40, confirmed by parsing the page's own in-page article-navigation index, which lists ids 1 through 40 with no gaps or duplicates), each in a clean, semantically-tagged

  • المادة ...

    ...
    block with no LLM summarization or paraphrase involved in extraction — the raw HTML was parsed programmatically (regex-based tag stripping, HTML-entity unescaping,
    -> newline, and a dedicated table-to-text converter for the two articles containing embedded HTML markup, described below). A final cleaning pass removed decorative in-word tatweel characters (U+0640) that appear between two Arabic letters inside otherwise-ordinary words -- a known Word/HTML full-justification artifact affecting Articles 2 and 13 (e.g. 'اسـم' -> 'اسم', 'رقـما' -> 'رقما') -- using the same before/after-Arabic-letter detection rule as this corpus's existing anti_narcotics (base law) validator's _bad_tatweel check; tatweels used as a genuine standalone list-letter styling convention (e.g. 'جـ –' for the isolated form of the letter ج) were left untouched since they are followed by a space, not another letter, and so do not match the in-word corruption pattern. This is a typographic-noise cleanup, not a change to any word's semantic content. nezams.com's own page metadata (Open Graph description) independently states: 'تاريخ اللائحة 10/06/1431هـ، الاعتماد – قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم 201 بتاريخ 10/06/1431هـ، تاريخ النشر 06/07/1431هـ، النفاذ: ساري، التعديلات: لم يجر عليها تعديل' (regulation date 10/6/1431H; approval CoM Resolution 201 dated 10/6/1431H; publication date 6/7/1431H; status: in force; amendments: none to date) — corroborating both dates and the no-amendments conclusion independently of the article body text itself. CROSS-VERIFICATION (PARTIAL, NOT FULL-TEXT): qistas.com's regulation page (fetched directly via curl with a browser User-Agent; HTTP 200) is a JavaScript-rendered preview that server-side-renders only its own first labeled 'Article 1' — which qistas.com's own markup actually contains the ENACTING RESOLUTION TEXT (the '١- الموافقة ... ٢- تعديل قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم 203 ...' passage), word-for-word identical (save for Western vs. Eastern Arabic-Indic digit style) to the preamble independently extracted from nezams.com, truncated mid-sentence at '... د- ألا يكون اشتراك ممثل ......' by qistas.com's own content-gating (a 'لاستعراض التشريع كاملاً' / 'view full legislation' call-to-action follows). This gives a genuine independent word-for-word match for the enacting-resolution preamble only — it does NOT reach any of the 40 substantive مواد of the Implementing Regulation itself, which remain SINGLE-SOURCED to nezams.com. almehleky.sa, a Saudi law-firm blog page (fetched via curl, HTTP 200), was also checked and paraphrases (in its own prose, not verbatim quotation) the subject matter of Articles 2, 20, and 34 in a manner consistent with nezams.com's extracted text (medical-transport drug quantities in Art. 2; prescription requirements in Art. 20; the threshold-quantity substance table in Art. 34) — a topical corroboration only, not a verbatim cross-check. A fourth source, a combined law+regulation reference PDF hosted at zarah.com.sa (fetched successfully via curl, HTTP 200, 372KB), was examined via pdftotext but rejected as USABLE evidence: its extracted text exhibits systematic Arabic ligature/digit-reversal corruption characteristic of a custom PDF font subset lacking a proper ToUnicode CMap (e.g. 'الله' extracts as 'اهلل'; the decree number 'م/39' extracts as 'م/93'; hijri year '1426' extracts as '6241' — a simple character-order reversal, but pervasive and unreliable to auto-correct without risking silent corruption elsewhere), making it unfit for verbatim quotation under this corpus's no-paraphrase/no-silent-correction rule; and (2) — independently of the corruption issue — this specific PDF's content terminates after the base law's Article 74 and does not actually contain the Implementing Regulation's own text at all, despite the filename referencing 'ولائحته التنفيذية'. It was therefore not used for cross-verification of any Regulation article, and is documented here only to show the fallback was attempted and why it was rejected. HONEST TIER DISCLOSURE: unlike the base law track (BOE_PROXY_X_NEZAMS_X_QADHA_REFERENCE_TRIPLE_VERIFIED, with all 74 articles resting on at least two independently-sourced full-text copies), this Implementing Regulation track rests on ONE full-text primary source (nezams.com) whose article bodies (all 40 مواد) were NOT independently corroborated word-for-word against a second full-text copy — only the enacting-resolution preamble (not any of the 40 مواد) was independently matched via qistas.com, and only topical/subject-matter (not verbatim) corroboration was obtained for 3 of the 40 articles via almehleky.sa. This is a materially lower verification tier than the base law's, and is disclosed explicitly here and in every known_unresolved_discrepancies entry and generator/validator docstring, per the corpus's binding trust rule that an honest 'could not achieve full independent verification' is required rather than overstating confidence. STRUCTURE: the atomic unit ingested is the source's own smallest independently-numbered division — the مادة (article), of which there are exactly 40, numbered 1 to 40 in a flat sequence with NO باب (Part) / فصل (Chapter) structure and — unlike the base law — NO unnumbered topical section headers either; nezams.com's rendering groups all 40 مواد under a single undifferentiated 'المواد' heading with no sub-grouping markup of any kind, so chapter_structure/section_ar fields are correctly and honestly left absent from this track rather than invented. This regulation is NOT organized as a substance schedule/list (قائمة) in its own top-level structure, despite its colloquial name 'القائمة التنفيذية' — the substance/dosage TABLES that do exist (in Articles 2 and 34 only) are embedded WITHIN two of the 40 numbered مواد as HTML
    elements in the source, not a freestanding schedule structure; they were converted to a linearized '[جدول] row1col1 | row1col2 ... [/جدول]' plain-text representation (a structural/formatting transform only, preserving every cell's exact original content — including bilingual Arabic/English drug names as published by the government's own text, not translations added by this track) so the full governing content of those two articles is retained without loss. Article 34 carries a trailing nezams.com-authored navigational sentence ('للاطلاع على الأحكام العامة على الجداول المرفقة ... انقر هنا [مرفق]', i.e. 'click here to view the attachment') pointing to an unrelated supplementary PDF hosted by nezams.com itself — this is a website editorial addition, not government legal text, and was excluded from the ingested article_text. AMENDMENT STATUS: nezams.com's own page metadata states 'التعديلات: لم يجر عليها تعديل' (no amendments made to date) as of the page's last-modified timestamp (2022-08-06, per its article:modified_time meta tag); no Royal Decree or Council of Ministers Resolution amending this Regulation's own 40 articles was found via WebSearch. All 40 articles are classified اصلية (original/unamended); none ملغاة (repealed) or مضافة (added). This rests on the same category of convergent-negative-evidence reasoning as the base law's amendment-history conclusion, and is flagged with the same category of residual verification gap. See sources/anti_narcotics/law/official_source/anti_narcotics_law_official_source.json for the base law's own 74-article methodology note, cross-referenced throughout this Regulation's article texts.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: MATERIAL TIER GAP (the most important disclosure in this track): all 40 مواد rest on a SINGLE full-text primary source (nezams.com), not the two-or-three-independent-source standard achieved for the base law (anti_narcotics, 74/74 articles BOE x nezams.com, penalty articles x qadha.org.sa reference book). The official BOE portal, the MOI PDF, and Wayback Machine content were all attempted and all failed (documented below in dedicated entries). qistas.com independently matched only the enacting-resolution PREAMBLE (not any of the 40 مواد themselves), word-for-word except for Eastern vs. Western Arabic-Indic digit style. almehleky.sa gave topical (not verbatim) corroboration for 3 of 40 articles (2, 20, 34). This is disclosed honestly rather than overstating this track's confidence to match the base law's tier.

The official BOE portal (laws.boe.gov.sa, lawId be479758-9a84-4e94-b1d3-a9a700f19454) could not be reached by any method attempted: WebFetch returned HTTP 503 on the LawDetails URL; a direct curl request (with a standard browser User-Agent, routed through the sandbox's HTTPS proxy) was reset by the server ('Recv failure: Connection reset by peer'); the r.jina.ai reader-proxy returned HTTP 422/401 on repeated attempts. This mirrors the exact same failure the base law's track documented for the same portal.

The MOI-hosted PDF ('Executive list for drugs.pdf', moi.gov.sa/wps/wcm/connect/1ee05af9-76be-46c8-82cf-6b4b86057d8c/...) could not be retrieved: WebFetch returned HTTP 503; a direct curl request was reset by the server ('Recv failure: Connection reset by peer') on every attempt. Its existence and URL are independently confirmed via WebSearch results (title: 'الالئحة التنفيذية لنظام مكافحة المخدرات والمؤثرات العقلية 1431 هـ'), but its content was never opened.

The archive.org 'wayback/available' API (a different host/endpoint, NOT blocked) confirmed a snapshot of the BOE LawDetails page exists, timestamped 20260209114130 (9 Feb 2026). Retrieving that snapshot's actual content failed via every method attempted: WebFetch returned HTTP 422 or refused the host outright; a direct curl request to web.archive.org (both the plain and the 'if_'-suffixed iframe-content URL forms) returned 'Blocked by egress policy' — a sandbox-level network restriction distinct from, and stricter than, the HTTPS proxy used for all other fetches in this track. This is the same category of gap the base law's track documented for the same archive.

A combined law+regulation reference PDF hosted at zarah.com.sa was fetched successfully (HTTP 200, 372KB) and examined via pdftotext, but deliberately excluded from use: (1) its extraction exhibits systematic Arabic ligature/digit-reversal corruption typical of a custom PDF font subset lacking a proper ToUnicode CMap (e.g. 'الله' renders as 'اهلل'; the decree number 'م/39' renders as 'م/93'; the hijri year '1426' renders as '6241' — a simple character-order reversal, but pervasive and unreliable to auto-correct without risking silent corruption elsewhere), making it unfit for verbatim quotation under this corpus's no-paraphrase/no-silent-correction rule; and (2) — independently of the corruption issue — this specific PDF's content terminates after the base law's Article 74 and does not actually contain the Implementing Regulation's own text at all, despite the filename referencing 'ولائحته التنفيذية'. It was therefore not used for cross-verification of any Regulation article, and is documented here only to show the fallback was attempted and why it was rejected.

Unlike the base law (anti_narcotics), which has unnumbered topical headers interspersed among its 74 articles (modeled in that track's chapter_structure), this Implementing Regulation's primary source (nezams.com) presents all 40 مواد under a single undifferentiated 'المواد' heading with no sub-grouping markup, no باب/فصل labels, and no topical section headers of any kind. chapter_structure and section_ar fields are therefore correctly and honestly OMITTED from this track rather than invented; this is a genuine structural difference from the base law, not an extraction oversight.

Article 34, as rendered on nezams.com, carries a trailing sentence — 'للاطلاع على الأحكام العامة على الجداول المرفقة بنظام مكافحة المخدرات والمؤثرات العقلية انقر هنا [مرفق]' ('click here to view the attachment') — linking to a separate supplementary PDF hosted by nezams.com itself. This is a website editorial/navigational addition, not government-issued legal text, and was excluded from the ingested article_text for anti_narcotics_regulation_art_034. Documented here rather than silently dropped.

Articles 2 and 34 contain data originally published as HTML <table> markup on the primary source (Article 2: two tables — permitted transport medicines, and per-passenger/per-trip-duration dosage ceilings; Article 34: one 33-row table of substances and their Article-47(paragraph 3)-referenced threshold quantities, giving Arabic and English/scientific drug names side by side as published). These were converted to a linearized plain-text '[جدول]\nrow1col1 | row1col2 | ...\n[/جدول]' representation to preserve every cell's exact content in a JSON-string-safe form — a structural/formatting transform only (not a translation, paraphrase, or content change); the bilingual Arabic/English drug nomenclature is exactly as published in the government's own table, not added by this track. Table row/column borders, cell widths, and other purely visual HTML styling attributes were discarded as non-textual formatting, not governing content.

nezams.com's HTML rendering consistently uses an en-dash character '–' (Unicode U+2013, HTML entity –) as a separator between numbered/lettered sub-item markers and their text throughout most of the 40 articles' body text, whereas the enacting Council of Ministers resolution's own preamble (also on the same nezams.com page) instead uses the Arabic tatweel-like dash 'ـ' in the analogous position ('أ ـ ألا يتجاوز...'). Because no second full-text source was available to cross-check which typographic mark (if any) the actual Official Gazette printing uses at each point, this en-dash styling is preserved verbatim as extracted rather than normalized or guessed at; it is disclosed as a low-stakes formatting uncertainty, not a substantive textual question.

Council of Ministers Resolution No. 201 (10/6/1431H) — the instrument that approved this Implementing Regulation — also contains a second, textually separate operative clause amending a DIFFERENT prior resolution (Council of Ministers Resolution No. 203, 14/7/1425H, as amended by No. 186, 17/7/1426H) to set/revise reward payments for members of the narcotics-destruction committee (لجنة إتلاف المخدرات) and to establish a monitoring committee at the Ministry of Interior. This reward-schedule text is reproduced in full in this artifact's preamble_ar field for transparency, but is NOT one of the Implementing Regulation's own 40 مواد and was NOT ingested as an article record — it amends a different instrument entirely.

Articles 2 and 13, as rendered by nezams.com, contained decorative in-word tatweel characters (U+0640) inserted purely for HTML/Word-style full-justification stretching -- e.g. 'اسـم' for 'اسم' (name), 'العبـوة' for 'العبوة' (packaging), 'رقـما' for 'رقما' (numerically), 'وكتـابة' for 'وكتابة' (in writing), 'واسـم' for 'واسم', 'الجهـة' for 'الجهة' (the entity). These were removed using the same before/after-Arabic-letter detection rule this corpus's base-law validator (anti_narcotics) already applies as its bad-tatweel quality bar, so this track meets the same text-quality standard. This is a typographic-noise cleanup only -- no word's semantic content changed -- and is disclosed here rather than silently applied. Tatweels used as genuine list-letter styling (e.g. 'جـ –' for the standalone letter ج) were left untouched, since they are followed by a space rather than another letter and so are not matched by the same rule.
